name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+30 partisan lean in a deep-blue suburban Maryland district
Raskin's incumbency and $7.9 million war chest versus Riley's $16,600 raised
Polymarket prices Raskin at 97% to win
model.rationale: The district's D+30 lean, Raskin's incumbency, and a massive financial advantage over a barely funded challenger all point to an easy Democratic hold, and markets agree at roughly 97% Democratic odds. No polls or expert ratings exist, but nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from a Safe D call.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing the Republican challenger within single digits would warrant revisiting, though no such evidence exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jamie Raskin seeks another term in this heavily Democratic Montgomery County-area district, where the partisan lean is D+30. He enters with roughly $7.9 million on hand after raising over $7.4 million, while Republican Cheryl Riley has raised about $16,600 with minimal cash remaining and no outside spending on either side. A Green candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no fundraising activity.

Prediction markets price Raskin's chances at about 97%, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic win.
